slides.headline: He sold a company he built from scratch for over nine billion dollars - the largest software deal of its time.
Romesh Wadhwani
slides.body: Born in Karachi, his family moved to India after Partition. He studied at IIT Bombay before earning a PhD from Carnegie Mellon, then moved to the US to build his career in enterprise software.

slides.headline: Aspect Development, sold for $9.3 billion in 1999.
slides.body: Wadhwani founded Aspect Development in Silicon Valley in 1991. Eight years later, i2 Technologies acquired it for $9.3 billion in stock - at the time, the Wall Street Journal called it the largest software deal ever made.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: IIT Bombay's returns compound for decades.
slides.body: Wadhwani went on to found Symphony Technology Group and Symphony AI, and now runs the Wadhwani Foundation, funding economic development back in India. One engineering degree, three decades, and a company sold for nine billion dollars - proof of what an IIT education abroad can turn into.

sources: CNBC, Dec 8, 2023 - How a 75-year-old Indian-American tech entrepreneur is betting $1 billion of his own fortune on AI's future
